title: Settings-driven paging and a read-only switch with Depends
problem: feed_api.py has finished routes that use three dependencies you must write: get_settings (configuration from the environment, built once), page_size (the request's page size, bounded by the settings) and require_writable (blocks writes in read-only mode).
requirements: get_settings() builds Settings from the environment variables in ENV_VARS that are set (others keep their defaults), converts them with the model, and is cached with lru_cache
An invalid environment value (e.g. FEED_PAGE_SIZE_MAX=lots) raises pydantic.ValidationError
page_size depends on get_settings and takes the optional query parameter limit
Without limit: settings.page_size_default. With limit: must be 1..settings.page_size_max inclusive, else HTTPException 422 with detail "limit must be between 1 and <max>"
require_writable raises HTTPException 503 with detail "feed is read-only" when settings.read_only is true; otherwise it does nothing
contract: get_settings() -> Settings (cached); page_size(settings, limit: int | None = None) -> int; require_writable(settings) -> None
expectedBehavior: GET /feed -> limit 20 and posts 250, 249, ...; with page_size_max=10: GET /feed?limit=11 -> 422 {"detail": "limit must be between 1 and 10"}; with read_only=True: POST /feed -> 503, GET /feed still 200
edgeCases: limit exactly page_size_max and limit 1 are valid; 0 and negatives are not
No environment variables at all gives Settings() with defaults
Changing the environment after the first call has no effect until cache_clear()
A blocked POST must not store anything
hints: Conceptual: get_settings is the only function that reads the environment. The other two only receive a Settings object, which is why the tests can swap it with dependency_overrides.

Specific: decorate get_settings with @lru_cache and build a dict of only the variables present, mapped to field names, then Settings.model_validate(that_dict). In page_size, handle limit is None first, then the range check.

Implementation: {field: os.environ[var] for var, field in ENV_VARS.items() if var in os.environ}; the range check is `if not 1 <= limit <= settings.page_size_max: raise HTTPException(status_code=422, detail=f"...")`; require_writable is two lines.
